bull_bear.body: The most checkable — and least comfortable — thread on the call. Operating cash flow has been **"negative for the last two years, despite profit growth"**, and management does not expect that to reverse this year: "We believe even this year we would have a large consumption of cash." The stated cause is growth investment, not collections: "It is not that we have had any challenges in our collections." Funding will be **"a mixture of our own internal accruals to finance the growth as well as external funds"** — i.e. external funding is now on the table for a company sitting on **₹356 Crores of cash and investments**. Asked whether Borqs is the sink, the CFO widened it: "It is just not Borqs, it is across as some of these engagements need working capital both in terms of capacity expansion as well as in terms of receivable and inventory." No dividend, buyback or debt commentary was offered. Inorganic spend remains possible ("we may look inorganic for our opportunities").
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Product Solutions margin at 5.9% with a contested bridge.** The 310bps-vs-690bps discrepancy (§2 box) means the size of the fall is not established. Management's own remedy is time, not action-specific: "we should look at the margins on a full year basis."
- **Memory shortage / component pricing is an active, unresolved input shock.** It hit margin (pass-through without carry), cash (inventory build) and, per Hareesh, customer behaviour — "on-device AI and memory supply pressure are reshaping product economics and encouraging customers to prioritize higher value enterprise and specialized devices."
- **Two years of negative operating cash flow, a third guided, plus "external funds."** With PAT at ₹23 Crores a quarter, an extended cash burn funded externally is the balance-sheet risk that most deserves next-quarter verification.
- **60x4x3 is slipping and management has softened it twice.** "Of course, three years was metaphoric. We may take maybe one or two more years." An analyst noted the $4m-plus customer count "has been at six for four consecutive quarters" — the count has not moved in a year while the deadline has.
- **Concentration is rising, not falling.** Top-5 at ~56% (analyst: up from 52%) — the *opposite* of what an account-broadening mission should produce, even as total customers went 79 → 93.
- **Disclosure opacity.** No vertical/offering revenue split ("We do not disclose number based on offerings or verticals"), no order backlog, no silicon production-vs-services split, no guidance, and no quantification of the foundry certifications. An analyst said so directly: "most of the IT companies would disclose their revenue segments it would be great if in future we can have that disclosure also."
- **Foundry certifications are unverifiable.** Intel and TSMC status is "in progress… we cannot specifically make any announcements on those yet."
- **Two-wheeler module opportunity is stuck on cost, not capability.** "We have the module ready, but then because of the cost, which the Quectel of the world gives, they are very cost sensitive, and they are taking it from China. So, we will have to see if there is any movement which will prevent them from importing these Chinese modules." The trigger is policy, and it is outside Sasken's control.
- **AI as a deflator of the headcount→revenue link.** "Headcount may not be the only vector to measure growth. So that will morph and we will have to look at how other metrics can be used" — the traditional visibility proxy for a services business is being retired without a replacement metric offered.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Notably more open than the disclosure record suggests: Mody opened by saying the company deliberately started these quarterly calls because "we felt it equally important to strengthen how we engage with the investment community" — this is a company newly courting the market, and the analyst list (Niveshaay, Vallum, Nuvama AMC, Bowhead, CARE PMS, TPF, ithought) reflects that. Candour is real on the awkward items: the 60x4x3 timeline slip was conceded unprompted; the negative cash flow was answered directly with the cause and the funding plan rather than deflected; and Hareesh gave a genuinely unflattering answer on two-wheeler modules (ready product, losing on Chinese cost). Against that: the answers thin out precisely where numbers would bind — no segment splits, no backlog, no guidance, no margin trajectory, no quantification of the hyperscaler engagements or the foundry certifications, and Mody's answer on *how* 60x4x3 gets achieved was explicitly withheld ("I may not be able to describe that fully to you in absolute black and white"). One reply drifted into promotional register — "your Company today is more broad-based" — without answering the analyst's actual question on revenue contribution by offering.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The growth is now organic, and that is the buried headline.** The CFO's reconciliation is the cleanest fact on the call: end-Q1 FY26 headcount 2,200 **already included** the ~300 Borqs people, and today's 2,658 means **"all of that growth is actually organic addition to headcount."** The 24% YoY revenue growth is therefore no longer an acquisition artefact — this is the first quarter where that can be said cleanly.
- **The margin problem and the strategic win are the same event.** Silicon "moving towards productization" is exactly what management wants (product ownership, longer programs) *and* is a named cause of the Product Solutions margin fall. Rising product mix will keep depressing percentage margin even when it is creating value — the wrong metric will look wrong for a while.
- **Pass-through protects revenue and destroys margin percentage.** Memory cost is passed on in full, so revenue is inflated by cost the company doesn't earn on. Product Solutions' +23.6% YoY revenue growth is, to an unquantified degree, memory price inflation flowing through — and the same mechanism is what drags the margin percentage down. Both segments printing "+20%+" is less clean than it reads.
- **Sasken is short-tenor by design and knows it.** TCV ≈ one quarter of revenue with a 9–10-month backlog carry means the sales engine must be refilled continuously; the 60x4x3 account-mining mission is the structural answer to that, which is why the slipping timeline matters more than it would at a peer with multi-year annuity contracts.
- **The Qualcomm reference-design story is a moat *and* a leak.** Sasken built the two-wheeler instrument-cluster reference design; "Qualcomm took it and gave it to all the module suppliers", and Quectel-type module makers built around it. Sasken created the IP and Chinese module makers monetise the volume — a precise illustration of why management wants to move from services to owned modules.
- **Top-5 concentration rising while customer count rises is the tell.** 79 → 93 customers but 52% → ~56% top-5 share means the large accounts are growing faster than the long tail — good for revenue quality, but it is the reverse of the 60x4x3 thesis of lifting the *middle* of the base to $4m.
- **AI is being sold as both the product and the delivery method.** "A large part of our business gets delivered through a combination of headcount and AI" — an ER&D firm using AI to deliver fixed-scope work is deliberately shrinking its own billable-hours base, which is why the headcount metric is being pre-emptively retired.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Over 30 years of operating history with multiple patents; has served over 100 Fortune 500 companies and powers over a billion devices through its services and IP
- Full-stack 'chip-to-cognition' engineering capability spanning silicon design, embedded platforms, automotive software, communications infrastructure, satellite ecosystems and digital engineering, positioning it to engage earlier in customers' design lifecycle

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Customer concentration — Revenue is concentrated in a small customer base: revenue from the top 2 customers was 20.78% of revenue in FY2025-26 (up from 17.15% in FY2024-25) and from the top 10 customers was 61.18% (up from 60.33%), so loss of or a slowdown at a handful of key accounts would be disproportionately impactful.
- Trade receivables / credit risk — Credit risk arises principally from trade receivables and unbilled revenue, which grew year-on-year (trade receivables `12,346.71 lakhs vs `9,295.32 lakhs, unbilled revenue `3,553.16 lakhs vs `2,721.47 lakhs), and receivables overdue beyond 180 days rose sharply to `155.59 lakhs from `16.13 lakhs a year earlier, indicating some deterioration in collection ageing even though no expected-credit-loss impairment was recognised.
- Foreign currency / export exposure — As an exporter of engineering services with the Indian Rupee as functional currency, the Company carries meaningful foreign-currency receivable/payable exposure across USD, EUR, JPY and CAD, making revenue and margins sensitive to currency movements.
- M&A integration risk (post-Borqs acquisition) — The Company updated its Risk Management Policy to address a broader and more complex risk landscape driven by its expansion into engineering services, silicon design and the ODM segment following the Borqs acquisition, explicitly flagging successful M&A integration as a risk area management is managing.
- Information security, cybersecurity and data privacy — The Company has had to fortify Information Security, Cybersecurity and Data Privacy processes under ISO 27001:2022 and ISO 27701:2019 with enhanced monitoring, preventive controls and incident response, reflecting the sensitivity of safeguarding customer and project data given the shift to hybrid and technology-enabled working models.
- Macro, regulatory and geopolitical uncertainty — Management explicitly cautions that actual results may differ materially due to changes in global economic conditions, customer spending patterns, regulatory developments, geopolitical factors, supply-chain dynamics and technology adoption cycles.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- **Software Services — ₹219 Crores, +24.3% YoY, +4.8% QoQ, GM 30.6% (+240bps).** The quarter's engine. Demand vectors named: automotive (software-defined vehicles, centralized compute architectures, 5G, V2X); communications infrastructure ("5G advanced, secure private networks, and AI-led network operations" with "recent engagement across massive MIMO, Beamforming, and Open RAN"); and digital/AI as "the horizontal, which is cutting across". Margin driver is operational, not pricing: utilization at 85%, cost discipline, scale.
- **Product Solutions (Borqs) — ₹120 Crores, +23.6% YoY, −3.9% QoQ, GM 5.9%.** The problem child and the strategic differentiator simultaneously. It "continued to navigate industry-wide pressures relating to memory availability, component pricing, and program mix". Strategically it is what converts Sasken from a services vendor into a product owner — "With Borqs integrated, we can support customers from concept and design through certifications, production, deployment, and after-sales service." Integration verdict from the CEO: "the Borqs acquisition has worked out really well for both Sasken and Borqs… we have integrated extremely well," with the benefit showing up in *services* too — "we have in services gotten engaged with larger customers because of our combined forces."
- **Sasken Silicon.** Explicitly **"early stage for us"**, being built "with a long-term perspective". Specialism is the scarce end of the stack: **"analog radio frequency millimeter wave design in which we specialize are very niche, hard to find and sought-after skill sets"** — grown in-house, "not just one level, but multiple levels deep". Demand is broadening from a niche component to a pervasive one: "we are migrating towards things like chiplets, things like memory integration, and… package design." It is also the reason Product Solutions margin moved — **"Our silicon business is moving towards productization and that has an impact on the margins."** Foundry relationships: GlobalFoundries IP certification confirmed previously; on Intel and a formal TSMC relationship — "All those three are in progress, and we have made substantial, significant progress… Due to the non-public nature of some of this progress… we cannot specifically make any announcements on those yet."

business.body:
- **Scarce analog/RF/mmWave design talent, built in-house.** "Analog radio frequency millimeter wave design in which we specialize are very niche, hard to find and sought-after skill sets. So, we've grown a lot of these in-house" — and the teams "operate independently", "not just one level, but multiple levels deep". This is a supply-side barrier, and Savla independently framed the market side of it: "analog and mixed signal engineering remain highly specialized domains where experience talent is scarce, pushing companies to look for partners with deep specialized design expertise rather than building everything in-house."
- **Full-stack span (silicon → device → cloud/AI) is what wins the logo.** "This experience has definitely brought in new customers to us because now whenever Rajiv and I, we went to meet the customers, all our customers like this idea of Sasken now becoming a full-fledged product engineering company… that is the reason we got some new wins as well."
- **Marquee installed base.** "We, as you know, serve most marquee customers globally. Fortune 500 plus Fortune 100, you name it, in the segments that we operate, we have them as our customers" — the 60x4x3 mission is an account-mining play on an existing base, not a new-logo hunt.
- **Delivery-led expansion.** "A lot of our engagements are also led by delivery… some of the growths that you see are also delivery led" — i.e. share gain inside accounts without proportionate sales cost.
- **Measured execution quality.** CSAT **4.5/5 vs a stated industry benchmark of 3.75**.

latest_quarter.body: Two opposite stories in one P&L. **Software Services margin is compounding** on utilization (85%), cost discipline and scale — and the CEO's framing of the multi-year move is the single most striking margin datapoint on the call: "in a matter of six quarters really turn around and improve the margins from maybe about 2%, and I am talking Software Services, maybe about 2% to 3% up to 11.5%, 12% EBIT." **Product Solutions margin is being compressed by pass-through economics** — the CFO's mechanism is precise and worth keeping: "memory pricing has an influence while we try and pass on everything to the customer. From a margin perspective, it affects because you do not get the same carry on the product as you would get earlier… you are passing on the cost, but the incremental margin does not come. So, from a percentage, it gets affected." The second driver is mix — Silicon "moving towards productization". On the headcount-vs-cost gap an analyst flagged (headcount +9%, cost +3%), the CFO attributed it to hiring mix (lateral + freshers), the non-recurring Q4 bonus catch-up, and improved utilization — "that is where you would have seen it not impacting the margins." Forward-looking cost adds already committed: "another five to six sales heads during the rest of the year".

outlook.body:
**Sasken explicitly gives no formal guidance** — "we do not give any guidance" (Rajiv Mody) and "we do not want to give any guidance on the margins at this point in time" (Priyaranjan). What was committed to directionally:
- **Revenue growth:** no number. Priority for the rest of FY2027 is "converting recent wins to sustainable revenues, improving execution consistency". Both segments "on a year-on-year basis has grown more than 20%".
- **Margin:** Product Solutions — "we should look at the margins on a full year basis to get a better picture. We believe that some of these actions which we have taken in Q1, we will see the margins starting to stabilize over the year." Group level — "the short answer is we will make sure that we will maintain our margins while we maintain our growth momentum."
- **Silicon:** "We do believe that we continue to show the growth rates which we have shown in the last year on Silicon, but we will not be able to give specific order breakdown."
- **Borqs break-even:** "the break-even point would be about 12 million revenue on a **quarterly** revenue. That is where we will hit the break-even point." (An analyst put the previously-stated figure at "$60, 70 million dollar top line" — the quarterly framing is consistent with that annualised.)
- **Order-book carry:** "we tend to make sure that the order backlog which we have does give us a carry of 9 to 10 months."
- **Sales capacity:** "we expect to add at least another five to six sales heads during the rest of the year."
- **Cash flow:** "We believe even this year we would have a large consumption of cash… we will use a mixture of our own internal accruals to finance the growth as well as external funds."
- **60x4x3 mission (60 customers × $4m run-rate × 3 years):** "this first quarter is the end of, out of the 12 quarters, 9th quarter"; timeline slipping — "Of course, three years was metaphoric. We may take maybe one or two more years, but the strategy remains intact."
- **Capex/commissioning:** none disclosed. Only footprint additions named: **Sasken Silicon Incubation Center, Hubballi** (inaugurated) and a **new centre of excellence in Hyderabad** (opened) — no cost, capacity or date.

Named wins this quarter: a **multi-year capability engagement with a global hyperscaler**, and **"a strategic engagement with a global technology Company to deliver services on AI and automation, spanning agentic AI, LLM validation, and intelligent testing."** On the two hyperscaler engagements disclosed (next-gen device across platforms; OS sustenance), management confirmed **"These are different hyperscaler."** Customer count moved **79 → 93** with **five new logos**; top-5 concentration ~56% (an analyst noted this is *up* from 52%). > **Adjustments / one-offs — call these out:**
> (a) **PAT's sequential fall is a Q4 base effect, not an operating miss** — "Sequential moderation impact was due to normalization of one-off benefits recorded in other income during Q4. Foreign exchange gains in the current quarter were lower compared to the previous quarter, which had benefited from favorable currency movements."
> (b) **Q4 FY26 cost base was inflated by bonus catch-up** — "there will be certain costs which would have probably come in Q4 due to catch up of bonuses which will not be recurring." This flatters the Q1 QoQ cost comparison.
> (c) **Product Solutions margin — two incompatible numbers are on the record.** The CFO said it "moderated to 5.9%, declining by 310 basis points sequentially"; the first analyst framed it as a "drop in Product Solutions margin from 12.8 to 5.9" (i.e. ~690bps) and management did not correct him. Do not use either as settled until the next disclosure.
> (d) **₹31 Crores EBITDA on ₹339 Crores revenue does not tie to the stated 9.5%** (implies ~9.1%). Rounding is the likely cause; both figures are quoted as given.
> (e) **Order book number is a flow, not a stock** — "when we publish the order book summary, it is the order booked in the quarter. It is not the total order backlog which we have."
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
**Sasken explicitly gives no formal guidance** — "we do not give any guidance" (Rajiv Mody) and "we do not want to give any guidance on the margins at this point in time" (Priyaranjan). What was committed to directionally:
- **Revenue growth:** no number. Priority for the rest of FY2027 is "converting recent wins to sustainable revenues, improving execution consistency". Both segments "on a year-on-year basis has grown more than 20%".
- **Margin:** Product Solutions — "we should look at the margins on a full year basis to get a better picture. We believe that some of these actions which we have taken in Q1, we will see the margins starting to stabilize over the year." Group level — "the short answer is we will make sure that we will maintain our margins while we maintain our growth momentum."
- **Silicon:** "We do believe that we continue to show the growth rates which we have shown in the last year on Silicon, but we will not be able to give specific order breakdown."
- **Borqs break-even:** "the break-even point would be about 12 million revenue on a **quarterly** revenue. That is where we will hit the break-even point." (An analyst put the previously-stated figure at "$60, 70 million dollar top line" — the quarterly framing is consistent with that annualised.)
- **Order-book carry:** "we tend to make sure that the order backlog which we have does give us a carry of 9 to 10 months."
- **Sales capacity:** "we expect to add at least another five to six sales heads during the rest of the year."
- **Cash flow:** "We believe even this year we would have a large consumption of cash… we will use a mixture of our own internal accruals to finance the growth as well as external funds."
- **60x4x3 mission (60 customers × $4m run-rate × 3 years):** "this first quarter is the end of, out of the 12 quarters, 9th quarter"; timeline slipping — "Of course, three years was metaphoric. We may take maybe one or two more years, but the strategy remains intact."
- **Capex/commissioning:** none disclosed. Only footprint additions named: **Sasken Silicon Incubation Center, Hubballi** (inaugurated) and a **new centre of excellence in Hyderabad** (opened) — no cost, capacity or date.
order book & pipeline: Order booking is disclosed as a quarterly **flow**: **TCV ~US$47 million** (US$34m new), **ACV ~US$40 million** (US$24m new), against a backlog policy of **"a carry of 9 to 10 months"**. An analyst pushed on exactly this — that a TCV of "$47 million… roughly comes to around a quarter of our revenue" is short-tenor versus peers running 9–12-month TCV — and the CFO's answer was that ACV is the delivery-relevant number and the backlog carry is the metric they manage to. Named wins this quarter: a **multi-year capability engagement with a global hyperscaler**, and **"a strategic engagement with a global technology Company to deliver services on AI and automation, spanning agentic AI, LLM validation, and intelligent testing."** On the two hyperscaler engagements disclosed (next-gen device across platforms; OS sustenance), management confirmed **"These are different hyperscaler."** Customer count moved **79 → 93** with **five new logos**; top-5 concentration ~56% (an analyst noted this is *up* from 52%). Silicon orders are **multi-year** and "a function of how the customer does the offtake"; no production-vs-services split will be given.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Software Services — ₹219 Crores, +24.3% YoY, +4.8% QoQ, GM 30.6% (+240bps).** The quarter's engine. Demand vectors named: automotive (software-defined vehicles, centralized compute architectures, 5G, V2X); communications infrastructure ("5G advanced, secure private networks, and AI-led network operations" with "recent engagement across massive MIMO, Beamforming, and Open RAN"); and digital/AI as "the horizontal, which is cutting across". Margin driver is operational, not pricing: utilization at 85%, cost discipline, scale.
- **Product Solutions (Borqs) — ₹120 Crores, +23.6% YoY, −3.9% QoQ, GM 5.9%.** The problem child and the strategic differentiator simultaneously. It "continued to navigate industry-wide pressures relating to memory availability, component pricing, and program mix". Strategically it is what converts Sasken from a services vendor into a product owner — "With Borqs integrated, we can support customers from concept and design through certifications, production, deployment, and after-sales service." Integration verdict from the CEO: "the Borqs acquisition has worked out really well for both Sasken and Borqs… we have integrated extremely well," with the benefit showing up in *services* too — "we have in services gotten engaged with larger customers because of our combined forces."
- **Sasken Silicon.** Explicitly **"early stage for us"**, being built "with a long-term perspective". Specialism is the scarce end of the stack: **"analog radio frequency millimeter wave design in which we specialize are very niche, hard to find and sought-after skill sets"** — grown in-house, "not just one level, but multiple levels deep". Demand is broadening from a niche component to a pervasive one: "we are migrating towards things like chiplets, things like memory integration, and… package design." It is also the reason Product Solutions margin moved — **"Our silicon business is moving towards productization and that has an impact on the margins."** Foundry relationships: GlobalFoundries IP certification confirmed previously; on Intel and a formal TSMC relationship — "All those three are in progress, and we have made substantial, significant progress… Due to the non-public nature of some of this progress… we cannot specifically make any announcements on those yet."
growth verticals / optionality:
- **AI-native engineering as a booked line, not a slide.** The strategic engagement covering "agentic AI, LLM validation, and intelligent testing" is a named, won engagement; management's blanket claim is "all the work that we do for largely for all our customers is AI led."
- **China+1 / Make-in-India product design.** "Make in India is another thing that is showing up in a big way where shifts are happening and customers outside, particularly European and US customers are asking for product to be fully designed, which is a China Plus One, or in many cases that the product cannot be done out of China."
- **IP licensing alongside services.** Asked directly whether an engineering-services company and an IP-licensing company inside one entity is a conflict, Mody said no — customers want partners who "help them do the IP development, including integrating their own IP"; Hareesh's example was the Qualcomm reference design where Sasken's IP flowed to module makers.
- **Module ownership beyond clusters.** "It need not be in the clusters. It could be in the NAD and other modules where people are expecting us to deliver modules to them."
- **Inorganic.** "Yes, there may be some gaps somewhere, which we may look inorganic for our opportunities over there" — no target, size or timeline.
- **Talent/geography build-out.** Hubballi Silicon Incubation Center (university collaboration, "development of future semiconductor talent") and a Hyderabad CoE "expanding our access to engineering talent".
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Scarce analog/RF/mmWave design talent, built in-house.** "Analog radio frequency millimeter wave design in which we specialize are very niche, hard to find and sought-after skill sets. So, we've grown a lot of these in-house" — and the teams "operate independently", "not just one level, but multiple levels deep". This is a supply-side barrier, and Savla independently framed the market side of it: "analog and mixed signal engineering remain highly specialized domains where experience talent is scarce, pushing companies to look for partners with deep specialized design expertise rather than building everything in-house."
- **Full-stack span (silicon → device → cloud/AI) is what wins the logo.** "This experience has definitely brought in new customers to us because now whenever Rajiv and I, we went to meet the customers, all our customers like this idea of Sasken now becoming a full-fledged product engineering company… that is the reason we got some new wins as well."
- **Marquee installed base.** "We, as you know, serve most marquee customers globally. Fortune 500 plus Fortune 100, you name it, in the segments that we operate, we have them as our customers" — the 60x4x3 mission is an account-mining play on an existing base, not a new-logo hunt.
- **Delivery-led expansion.** "A lot of our engagements are also led by delivery… some of the growths that you see are also delivery led" — i.e. share gain inside accounts without proportionate sales cost.
- **Measured execution quality.** CSAT **4.5/5 vs a stated industry benchmark of 3.75**.
margins & cost dynamics: Two opposite stories in one P&L. **Software Services margin is compounding** on utilization (85%), cost discipline and scale — and the CEO's framing of the multi-year move is the single most striking margin datapoint on the call: "in a matter of six quarters really turn around and improve the margins from maybe about 2%, and I am talking Software Services, maybe about 2% to 3% up to 11.5%, 12% EBIT." **Product Solutions margin is being compressed by pass-through economics** — the CFO's mechanism is precise and worth keeping: "memory pricing has an influence while we try and pass on everything to the customer. From a margin perspective, it affects because you do not get the same carry on the product as you would get earlier… you are passing on the cost, but the incremental margin does not come. So, from a percentage, it gets affected." The second driver is mix — Silicon "moving towards productization". On the headcount-vs-cost gap an analyst flagged (headcount +9%, cost +3%), the CFO attributed it to hiring mix (lateral + freshers), the non-recurring Q4 bonus catch-up, and improved utilization — "that is where you would have seen it not impacting the margins." Forward-looking cost adds already committed: "another five to six sales heads during the rest of the year".
capex / expansion (watch slippage): No capex number, no commissioning date and no capacity figure were disclosed on this call. Physical expansion named: **Sasken Silicon Incubation Center at Hubballi** (inaugurated, university collaboration) and a **new centre of excellence in Hyderabad** (opened). The only quantified balance-sheet consumption is working capital and fixed assets inside the cash-flow answer — "as we scale, there is going to be consumption in working capital as well as on FA" — plus a specific Q1 item: **"in Q1, we had to build some of the inventories in order to manage the memory shortage. So, in Q1, the cash flow impact is coming from there."**
capital allocation: The most checkable — and least comfortable — thread on the call. Operating cash flow has been **"negative for the last two years, despite profit growth"**, and management does not expect that to reverse this year: "We believe even this year we would have a large consumption of cash." The stated cause is growth investment, not collections: "It is not that we have had any challenges in our collections." Funding will be **"a mixture of our own internal accruals to finance the growth as well as external funds"** — i.e. external funding is now on the table for a company sitting on **₹356 Crores of cash and investments**. Asked whether Borqs is the sink, the CFO widened it: "It is just not Borqs, it is across as some of these engagements need working capital both in terms of capacity expansion as well as in terms of receivable and inventory." No dividend, buyback or debt commentary was offered. Inorganic spend remains possible ("we may look inorganic for our opportunities").
risks & watch-items:
- **Product Solutions margin at 5.9% with a contested bridge.** The 310bps-vs-690bps discrepancy (§2 box) means the size of the fall is not established. Management's own remedy is time, not action-specific: "we should look at the margins on a full year basis."
- **Memory shortage / component pricing is an active, unresolved input shock.** It hit margin (pass-through without carry), cash (inventory build) and, per Hareesh, customer behaviour — "on-device AI and memory supply pressure are reshaping product economics and encouraging customers to prioritize higher value enterprise and specialized devices."
- **Two years of negative operating cash flow, a third guided, plus "external funds."** With PAT at ₹23 Crores a quarter, an extended cash burn funded externally is the balance-sheet risk that most deserves next-quarter verification.
- **60x4x3 is slipping and management has softened it twice.** "Of course, three years was metaphoric. We may take maybe one or two more years." An analyst noted the $4m-plus customer count "has been at six for four consecutive quarters" — the count has not moved in a year while the deadline has.
- **Concentration is rising, not falling.** Top-5 at ~56% (analyst: up from 52%) — the *opposite* of what an account-broadening mission should produce, even as total customers went 79 → 93.
- **Disclosure opacity.** No vertical/offering revenue split ("We do not disclose number based on offerings or verticals"), no order backlog, no silicon production-vs-services split, no guidance, and no quantification of the foundry certifications. An analyst said so directly: "most of the IT companies would disclose their revenue segments it would be great if in future we can have that disclosure also."
- **Foundry certifications are unverifiable.** Intel and TSMC status is "in progress… we cannot specifically make any announcements on those yet."
- **Two-wheeler module opportunity is stuck on cost, not capability.** "We have the module ready, but then because of the cost, which the Quectel of the world gives, they are very cost sensitive, and they are taking it from China. So, we will have to see if there is any movement which will prevent them from importing these Chinese modules." The trigger is policy, and it is outside Sasken's control.
- **AI as a deflator of the headcount→revenue link.** "Headcount may not be the only vector to measure growth. So that will morph and we will have to look at how other metrics can be used" — the traditional visibility proxy for a services business is being retired without a replacement metric offered.
management quality / tone: Notably more open than the disclosure record suggests: Mody opened by saying the company deliberately started these quarterly calls because "we felt it equally important to strengthen how we engage with the investment community" — this is a company newly courting the market, and the analyst list (Niveshaay, Vallum, Nuvama AMC, Bowhead, CARE PMS, TPF, ithought) reflects that. Candour is real on the awkward items: the 60x4x3 timeline slip was conceded unprompted; the negative cash flow was answered directly with the cause and the funding plan rather than deflected; and Hareesh gave a genuinely unflattering answer on two-wheeler modules (ready product, losing on Chinese cost). Against that: the answers thin out precisely where numbers would bind — no segment splits, no backlog, no guidance, no margin trajectory, no quantification of the hyperscaler engagements or the foundry certifications, and Mody's answer on *how* 60x4x3 gets achieved was explicitly withheld ("I may not be able to describe that fully to you in absolute black and white"). One reply drifted into promotional register — "your Company today is more broad-based" — without answering the analyst's actual question on revenue contribution by offering.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The growth is now organic, and that is the buried headline.** The CFO's reconciliation is the cleanest fact on the call: end-Q1 FY26 headcount 2,200 **already included** the ~300 Borqs people, and today's 2,658 means **"all of that growth is actually organic addition to headcount."** The 24% YoY revenue growth is therefore no longer an acquisition artefact — this is the first quarter where that can be said cleanly.
- **The margin problem and the strategic win are the same event.** Silicon "moving towards productization" is exactly what management wants (product ownership, longer programs) *and* is a named cause of the Product Solutions margin fall. Rising product mix will keep depressing percentage margin even when it is creating value — the wrong metric will look wrong for a while.
- **Pass-through protects revenue and destroys margin percentage.** Memory cost is passed on in full, so revenue is inflated by cost the company doesn't earn on. Product Solutions' +23.6% YoY revenue growth is, to an unquantified degree, memory price inflation flowing through — and the same mechanism is what drags the margin percentage down. Both segments printing "+20%+" is less clean than it reads.
- **Sasken is short-tenor by design and knows it.** TCV ≈ one quarter of revenue with a 9–10-month backlog carry means the sales engine must be refilled continuously; the 60x4x3 account-mining mission is the structural answer to that, which is why the slipping timeline matters more than it would at a peer with multi-year annuity contracts.
- **The Qualcomm reference-design story is a moat *and* a leak.** Sasken built the two-wheeler instrument-cluster reference design; "Qualcomm took it and gave it to all the module suppliers", and Quectel-type module makers built around it. Sasken created the IP and Chinese module makers monetise the volume — a precise illustration of why management wants to move from services to owned modules.
- **Top-5 concentration rising while customer count rises is the tell.** 79 → 93 customers but 52% → ~56% top-5 share means the large accounts are growing faster than the long tail — good for revenue quality, but it is the reverse of the 60x4x3 thesis of lifting the *middle* of the base to $4m.
- **AI is being sold as both the product and the delivery method.** "A large part of our business gets delivered through a combination of headcount and AI" — an ER&D firm using AI to deliver fixed-scope work is deliberately shrinking its own billable-hours base, which is why the headcount metric is being pre-emptively retired.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Sasken is a specialist in Product Engineering and Digital Transformation, providing concept-to-market, chip-to-cognition R&D services to global leaders across Semiconductor, Automotive, Industrials, Smart Devices & Wearables, Enterprise Grade Devices, SatCom and Transportation industries.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Sasken provides end-to-end R&D and engineering services covering hardware design, embedded software, platform/application software, testing, and system integration for a predominantly B2B client base of global technology companies, OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers. Established in 1989 and listed since its 2005 IPO, the Company and its subsidiaries employ around 2,400 people operating from centers/offices in Bengaluru, Pune, Chennai, Ahmedabad, Hyderabad and Kolkata (India), with presence across Finland, Germany, Singapore, Japan, China, Hong Kong, Cayman Islands and USA.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Software Services — ₹219 Crores, +24.3% YoY, +4.8% QoQ, GM 30.6% (+240bps).** The quarter's engine. Demand vectors named: automotive (software-defined vehicles, centralized compute architectures, 5G, V2X); communications infrastructure ("5G advanced, secure private networks, and AI-led network operations" with "recent engagement across massive MIMO, Beamforming, and Open RAN"); and digital/AI as "the horizontal, which is cutting across". Margin driver is operational, not pricing: utilization at 85%, cost discipline, scale.
- **Product Solutions (Borqs) — ₹120 Crores, +23.6% YoY, −3.9% QoQ, GM 5.9%.** The problem child and the strategic differentiator simultaneously. It "continued to navigate industry-wide pressures relating to memory availability, component pricing, and program mix". Strategically it is what converts Sasken from a services vendor into a product owner — "With Borqs integrated, we can support customers from concept and design through certifications, production, deployment, and after-sales service." Integration verdict from the CEO: "the Borqs acquisition has worked out really well for both Sasken and Borqs… we have integrated extremely well," with the benefit showing up in *services* too — "we have in services gotten engaged with larger customers because of our combined forces."
- **Sasken Silicon.** Explicitly **"early stage for us"**, being built "with a long-term perspective". Specialism is the scarce end of the stack: **"analog radio frequency millimeter wave design in which we specialize are very niche, hard to find and sought-after skill sets"** — grown in-house, "not just one level, but multiple levels deep". Demand is broadening from a niche component to a pervasive one: "we are migrating towards things like chiplets, things like memory integration, and… package design." It is also the reason Product Solutions margin moved — **"Our silicon business is moving towards productization and that has an impact on the margins."** Foundry relationships: GlobalFoundries IP certification confirmed previously; on Intel and a formal TSMC relationship — "All those three are in progress, and we have made substantial, significant progress… Due to the non-public nature of some of this progress… we cannot specifically make any announcements on those yet."

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Order booking is disclosed as a quarterly **flow**: **TCV ~US$47 million** (US$34m new), **ACV ~US$40 million** (US$24m new), against a backlog policy of **"a carry of 9 to 10 months"**. An analyst pushed on exactly this — that a TCV of "$47 million… roughly comes to around a quarter of our revenue" is short-tenor versus peers running 9–12-month TCV — and the CFO's answer was that ACV is the delivery-relevant number and the backlog carry is the metric they manage to. Named wins this quarter: a **multi-year capability engagement with a global hyperscaler**, and **"a strategic engagement with a global technology Company to deliver services on AI and automation, spanning agentic AI, LLM validation, and intelligent testing."** On the two hyperscaler engagements disclosed (next-gen device across platforms; OS sustenance), management confirmed **"These are different hyperscaler."** Customer count moved **79 → 93** with **five new logos**; top-5 concentration ~56% (an analyst noted this is *up* from 52%). Silicon orders are **multi-year** and "a function of how the customer does the offtake"; no production-vs-services split will be given.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
**Sasken explicitly gives no formal guidance** — "we do not give any guidance" (Rajiv Mody) and "we do not want to give any guidance on the margins at this point in time" (Priyaranjan). What was committed to directionally:
- **Revenue growth:** no number. Priority for the rest of FY2027 is "converting recent wins to sustainable revenues, improving execution consistency". Both segments "on a year-on-year basis has grown more than 20%".
- **Margin:** Product Solutions — "we should look at the margins on a full year basis to get a better picture. We believe that some of these actions which we have taken in Q1, we will see the margins starting to stabilize over the year." Group level — "the short answer is we will make sure that we will maintain our margins while we maintain our growth momentum."
- **Silicon:** "We do believe that we continue to show the growth rates which we have shown in the last year on Silicon, but we will not be able to give specific order breakdown."
- **Borqs break-even:** "the break-even point would be about 12 million revenue on a **quarterly** revenue. That is where we will hit the break-even point." (An analyst put the previously-stated figure at "$60, 70 million dollar top line" — the quarterly framing is consistent with that annualised.)
- **Order-book carry:** "we tend to make sure that the order backlog which we have does give us a carry of 9 to 10 months."
- **Sales capacity:** "we expect to add at least another five to six sales heads during the rest of the year."
- **Cash flow:** "We believe even this year we would have a large consumption of cash… we will use a mixture of our own internal accruals to finance the growth as well as external funds."
- **60x4x3 mission (60 customers × $4m run-rate × 3 years):** "this first quarter is the end of, out of the 12 quarters, 9th quarter"; timeline slipping — "Of course, three years was metaphoric. We may take maybe one or two more years, but the strategy remains intact."
- **Capex/commissioning:** none disclosed. Only footprint additions named: **Sasken Silicon Incubation Center, Hubballi** (inaugurated) and a **new centre of excellence in Hyderabad** (opened) — no cost, capacity or date.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Sasken is an asset-light R&D/engineering services business; the AR discloses no physical plant, site or manufacturing-capacity expansion. Expansion is framed in capability terms: under its 'Depth over Breadth' strategy for FY2025-26, the Company shifted emphasis under the 60x4x3 framework from account/market expansion to deepening engagement quality, increasing wallet share within strategic accounts, and monetizing already-built capabilities. It also advanced GenAI initiatives, deploying agentic solutions within engineering workflows and reinforcing secure-by-design frameworks for safety-critical industries, alongside continued investment in talent and AI capability, which management describes as building 'a solid foundation for scale, resilience, and long-term sustainable value creation.' Separately, the Company holds ongoing capital commitments to two Category II Alternative Investment Funds (see capex_disclosed).

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Notably more open than the disclosure record suggests: Mody opened by saying the company deliberately started these quarterly calls because "we felt it equally important to strengthen how we engage with the investment community" — this is a company newly courting the market, and the analyst list (Niveshaay, Vallum, Nuvama AMC, Bowhead, CARE PMS, TPF, ithought) reflects that. Candour is real on the awkward items: the 60x4x3 timeline slip was conceded unprompted; the negative cash flow was answered directly with the cause and the funding plan rather than deflected; and Hareesh gave a genuinely unflattering answer on two-wheeler modules (ready product, losing on Chinese cost). Against that: the answers thin out precisely where numbers would bind — no segment splits, no backlog, no guidance, no margin trajectory, no quantification of the hyperscaler engagements or the foundry certifications, and Mody's answer on *how* 60x4x3 gets achieved was explicitly withheld ("I may not be able to describe that fully to you in absolute black and white"). One reply drifted into promotional register — "your Company today is more broad-based" — without answering the analyst's actual question on revenue contribution by offering.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Over 30 years of operating history with multiple patents; has served over 100 Fortune 500 companies and powers over a billion devices through its services and IP
- Full-stack 'chip-to-cognition' engineering capability spanning silicon design, embedded platforms, automotive software, communications infrastructure, satellite ecosystems and digital engineering, positioning it to engage earlier in customers' design lifecycle

- Broad international footprint (India plus Finland, Germany, Singapore, Japan, China, Hong Kong, Cayman Islands, USA) serving global OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers, with exports contributing the majority of turnover

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **Product Solutions margin at 5.9% with a contested bridge.** The 310bps-vs-690bps discrepancy (§2 box) means the size of the fall is not established. Management's own remedy is time, not action-specific: "we should look at the margins on a full year basis."
- **Memory shortage / component pricing is an active, unresolved input shock.** It hit margin (pass-through without carry), cash (inventory build) and, per Hareesh, customer behaviour — "on-device AI and memory supply pressure are reshaping product economics and encouraging customers to prioritize higher value enterprise and specialized devices."
- **Two years of negative operating cash flow, a third guided, plus "external funds."** With PAT at ₹23 Crores a quarter, an extended cash burn funded externally is the balance-sheet risk that most deserves next-quarter verification.
- **60x4x3 is slipping and management has softened it twice.** "Of course, three years was metaphoric. We may take maybe one or two more years." An analyst noted the $4m-plus customer count "has been at six for four consecutive quarters" — the count has not moved in a year while the deadline has.
- **Concentration is rising, not falling.** Top-5 at ~56% (analyst: up from 52%) — the *opposite* of what an account-broadening mission should produce, even as total customers went 79 → 93.
- **Disclosure opacity.** No vertical/offering revenue split ("We do not disclose number based on offerings or verticals"), no order backlog, no silicon production-vs-services split, no guidance, and no quantification of the foundry certifications. An analyst said so directly: "most of the IT companies would disclose their revenue segments it would be great if in future we can have that disclosure also."
- **Foundry certifications are unverifiable.** Intel and TSMC status is "in progress… we cannot specifically make any announcements on those yet."
- **Two-wheeler module opportunity is stuck on cost, not capability.** "We have the module ready, but then because of the cost, which the Quectel of the world gives, they are very cost sensitive, and they are taking it from China. So, we will have to see if there is any movement which will prevent them from importing these Chinese modules." The trigger is policy, and it is outside Sasken's control.
- **AI as a deflator of the headcount→revenue link.** "Headcount may not be the only vector to measure growth. So that will morph and we will have to look at how other metrics can be used" — the traditional visibility proxy for a services business is being retired without a replacement metric offered.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- **The growth is now organic, and that is the buried headline.** The CFO's reconciliation is the cleanest fact on the call: end-Q1 FY26 headcount 2,200 **already included** the ~300 Borqs people, and today's 2,658 means **"all of that growth is actually organic addition to headcount."** The 24% YoY revenue growth is therefore no longer an acquisition artefact — this is the first quarter where that can be said cleanly.
- **The margin problem and the strategic win are the same event.** Silicon "moving towards productization" is exactly what management wants (product ownership, longer programs) *and* is a named cause of the Product Solutions margin fall. Rising product mix will keep depressing percentage margin even when it is creating value — the wrong metric will look wrong for a while.
- **Pass-through protects revenue and destroys margin percentage.** Memory cost is passed on in full, so revenue is inflated by cost the company doesn't earn on. Product Solutions' +23.6% YoY revenue growth is, to an unquantified degree, memory price inflation flowing through — and the same mechanism is what drags the margin percentage down. Both segments printing "+20%+" is less clean than it reads.
- **Sasken is short-tenor by design and knows it.** TCV ≈ one quarter of revenue with a 9–10-month backlog carry means the sales engine must be refilled continuously; the 60x4x3 account-mining mission is the structural answer to that, which is why the slipping timeline matters more than it would at a peer with multi-year annuity contracts.
- **The Qualcomm reference-design story is a moat *and* a leak.** Sasken built the two-wheeler instrument-cluster reference design; "Qualcomm took it and gave it to all the module suppliers", and Quectel-type module makers built around it. Sasken created the IP and Chinese module makers monetise the volume — a precise illustration of why management wants to move from services to owned modules.
- **Top-5 concentration rising while customer count rises is the tell.** 79 → 93 customers but 52% → ~56% top-5 share means the large accounts are growing faster than the long tail — good for revenue quality, but it is the reverse of the 60x4x3 thesis of lifting the *middle* of the base to $4m.
- **AI is being sold as both the product and the delivery method.** "A large part of our business gets delivered through a combination of headcount and AI" — an ER&D firm using AI to deliver fixed-scope work is deliberately shrinking its own billable-hours base, which is why the headcount metric is being pre-emptively retired.

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)
qoq_log.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** First concall note — supersedes the identity-only `SASKEN_SK.md` profile. Revenue **₹339 Cr (+24% YoY, +1.6% QoQ)**; Software Services **₹219 Cr (+24.3%)** with GM **30.6% (+240bps)**; Product Solutions **₹120 Cr (+23.6% YoY, −3.9% QoQ)** with GM down to **5.9%**. EBITDA **₹31 Cr / 9.5%**, EBIT **₹21 Cr / 6.3% (+430bps YoY, −50bps QoQ)**, PAT **₹23 Cr / 6.9%** (QoQ fall = Q4 other-income one-off + lower FX gains). Order booking **TCV ~US$47m (US$34m new) / ACV ~US$40m (US$24m new)**; customers **79 → 93**, five new logos, top-5 ~**56%**; headcount **2,658** (attrition 9.8%, utilization 85%) with the entire post-Q1-FY26 addition **organic**; cash & investments **₹356 Cr**. New this quarter: multi-year **hyperscaler** capability engagement + a global-tech **agentic-AI / LLM-validation / intelligent-testing** engagement; **Hubballi** Silicon Incubation Center and **Hyderabad** CoE opened. Open items: **60x4x3 timeline slipped** ("one or two more years", 9 of 12 quarters done, $4m+ customers stuck at six for four quarters); **operating cash flow negative two years running with a third guided** and "external funds" contemplated; **Intel/TSMC** foundry relationships "in progress", non-public; Borqs break-even set at **~US$12m quarterly revenue**.
- _Q2 FY27 → check: did Product Solutions gross margin stabilise off 5.9% as promised (and which sequential-decline figure — 310bps or 690bps — the company stands behind); did memory availability/pricing ease and did the Q1 inventory build unwind; did operating cash flow turn, and was any "external funds" facility actually raised (size, instrument, cost); did the $4m+ customer count finally move off six; did top-5 concentration keep rising past 56%; did Software Services hold 30%+ gross margin at 85% utilization; were the five-to-six sales hires made; any announceable progress on Intel/TSMC; is Borqs approaching the ~US$12m quarterly break-even; did the two-wheeler module opportunity convert on any policy change._

one-line thesis: Sasken has stopped being a flat, ex-growth communications-engineering shop: consolidated revenue of **₹339 Crores, "increasing 24% year-on-year"**, with **both** segments above 20% YoY and software-services gross margin **"improved by 240-basis points to 30.6%"**. The engine is the two-year re-platforming — the Borqs ODM acquisition plus the Silicon build-out into a "Chip-to-Cognition" full-stack pitch — and it is now producing $47m of quarterly TCV and 93 active customers (vs 79). The two honest offsets: **Product Solutions margin collapsed to 5.9%** under memory-price pass-through and mix, and **operating cash flow "has been negative for the last two years"** with management guiding to "a large consumption of cash" again this year, part-funded by **"external funds"**.

guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
**Sasken explicitly gives no formal guidance** — "we do not give any guidance" (Rajiv Mody) and "we do not want to give any guidance on the margins at this point in time" (Priyaranjan). What was committed to directionally:
- **Revenue growth:** no number. Priority for the rest of FY2027 is "converting recent wins to sustainable revenues, improving execution consistency". Both segments "on a year-on-year basis has grown more than 20%".
- **Margin:** Product Solutions — "we should look at the margins on a full year basis to get a better picture. We believe that some of these actions which we have taken in Q1, we will see the margins starting to stabilize over the year." Group level — "the short answer is we will make sure that we will maintain our margins while we maintain our growth momentum."
- **Silicon:** "We do believe that we continue to show the growth rates which we have shown in the last year on Silicon, but we will not be able to give specific order breakdown."
- **Borqs break-even:** "the break-even point would be about 12 million revenue on a **quarterly** revenue. That is where we will hit the break-even point." (An analyst put the previously-stated figure at "$60, 70 million dollar top line" — the quarterly framing is consistent with that annualised.)
- **Order-book carry:** "we tend to make sure that the order backlog which we have does give us a carry of 9 to 10 months."
- **Sales capacity:** "we expect to add at least another five to six sales heads during the rest of the year."
- **Cash flow:** "We believe even this year we would have a large consumption of cash… we will use a mixture of our own internal accruals to finance the growth as well as external funds."
- **60x4x3 mission (60 customers × $4m run-rate × 3 years):** "this first quarter is the end of, out of the 12 quarters, 9th quarter"; timeline slipping — "Of course, three years was metaphoric. We may take maybe one or two more years, but the strategy remains intact."
- **Capex/commissioning:** none disclosed. Only footprint additions named: **Sasken Silicon Incubation Center, Hubballi** (inaugurated) and a **new centre of excellence in Hyderabad** (opened) — no cost, capacity or date.
order book & pipeline: Order booking is disclosed as a quarterly **flow**: **TCV ~US$47 million** (US$34m new), **ACV ~US$40 million** (US$24m new), against a backlog policy of **"a carry of 9 to 10 months"**. An analyst pushed on exactly this — that a TCV of "$47 million… roughly comes to around a quarter of our revenue" is short-tenor versus peers running 9–12-month TCV — and the CFO's answer was that ACV is the delivery-relevant number and the backlog carry is the metric they manage to. Named wins this quarter: a **multi-year capability engagement with a global hyperscaler**, and **"a strategic engagement with a global technology Company to deliver services on AI and automation, spanning agentic AI, LLM validation, and intelligent testing."** On the two hyperscaler engagements disclosed (next-gen device across platforms; OS sustenance), management confirmed **"These are different hyperscaler."** Customer count moved **79 → 93** with **five new logos**; top-5 concentration ~56% (an analyst noted this is *up* from 52%). Silicon orders are **multi-year** and "a function of how the customer does the offtake"; no production-vs-services split will be given.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Software Services — ₹219 Crores, +24.3% YoY, +4.8% QoQ, GM 30.6% (+240bps).** The quarter's engine. Demand vectors named: automotive (software-defined vehicles, centralized compute architectures, 5G, V2X); communications infrastructure ("5G advanced, secure private networks, and AI-led network operations" with "recent engagement across massive MIMO, Beamforming, and Open RAN"); and digital/AI as "the horizontal, which is cutting across". Margin driver is operational, not pricing: utilization at 85%, cost discipline, scale.
- **Product Solutions (Borqs) — ₹120 Crores, +23.6% YoY, −3.9% QoQ, GM 5.9%.** The problem child and the strategic differentiator simultaneously. It "continued to navigate industry-wide pressures relating to memory availability, component pricing, and program mix". Strategically it is what converts Sasken from a services vendor into a product owner — "With Borqs integrated, we can support customers from concept and design through certifications, production, deployment, and after-sales service." Integration verdict from the CEO: "the Borqs acquisition has worked out really well for both Sasken and Borqs… we have integrated extremely well," with the benefit showing up in *services* too — "we have in services gotten engaged with larger customers because of our combined forces."
- **Sasken Silicon.** Explicitly **"early stage for us"**, being built "with a long-term perspective". Specialism is the scarce end of the stack: **"analog radio frequency millimeter wave design in which we specialize are very niche, hard to find and sought-after skill sets"** — grown in-house, "not just one level, but multiple levels deep". Demand is broadening from a niche component to a pervasive one: "we are migrating towards things like chiplets, things like memory integration, and… package design." It is also the reason Product Solutions margin moved — **"Our silicon business is moving towards productization and that has an impact on the margins."** Foundry relationships: GlobalFoundries IP certification confirmed previously; on Intel and a formal TSMC relationship — "All those three are in progress, and we have made substantial, significant progress… Due to the non-public nature of some of this progress… we cannot specifically make any announcements on those yet."
growth verticals / optionality:
- **AI-native engineering as a booked line, not a slide.** The strategic engagement covering "agentic AI, LLM validation, and intelligent testing" is a named, won engagement; management's blanket claim is "all the work that we do for largely for all our customers is AI led."
- **China+1 / Make-in-India product design.** "Make in India is another thing that is showing up in a big way where shifts are happening and customers outside, particularly European and US customers are asking for product to be fully designed, which is a China Plus One, or in many cases that the product cannot be done out of China."
- **IP licensing alongside services.** Asked directly whether an engineering-services company and an IP-licensing company inside one entity is a conflict, Mody said no — customers want partners who "help them do the IP development, including integrating their own IP"; Hareesh's example was the Qualcomm reference design where Sasken's IP flowed to module makers.
- **Module ownership beyond clusters.** "It need not be in the clusters. It could be in the NAD and other modules where people are expecting us to deliver modules to them."
- **Inorganic.** "Yes, there may be some gaps somewhere, which we may look inorganic for our opportunities over there" — no target, size or timeline.
- **Talent/geography build-out.** Hubballi Silicon Incubation Center (university collaboration, "development of future semiconductor talent") and a Hyderabad CoE "expanding our access to engineering talent".
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Scarce analog/RF/mmWave design talent, built in-house.** "Analog radio frequency millimeter wave design in which we specialize are very niche, hard to find and sought-after skill sets. So, we've grown a lot of these in-house" — and the teams "operate independently", "not just one level, but multiple levels deep". This is a supply-side barrier, and Savla independently framed the market side of it: "analog and mixed signal engineering remain highly specialized domains where experience talent is scarce, pushing companies to look for partners with deep specialized design expertise rather than building everything in-house."
- **Full-stack span (silicon → device → cloud/AI) is what wins the logo.** "This experience has definitely brought in new customers to us because now whenever Rajiv and I, we went to meet the customers, all our customers like this idea of Sasken now becoming a full-fledged product engineering company… that is the reason we got some new wins as well."
- **Marquee installed base.** "We, as you know, serve most marquee customers globally. Fortune 500 plus Fortune 100, you name it, in the segments that we operate, we have them as our customers" — the 60x4x3 mission is an account-mining play on an existing base, not a new-logo hunt.
- **Delivery-led expansion.** "A lot of our engagements are also led by delivery… some of the growths that you see are also delivery led" — i.e. share gain inside accounts without proportionate sales cost.
- **Measured execution quality.** CSAT **4.5/5 vs a stated industry benchmark of 3.75**.
margins & cost dynamics: Two opposite stories in one P&L. **Software Services margin is compounding** on utilization (85%), cost discipline and scale — and the CEO's framing of the multi-year move is the single most striking margin datapoint on the call: "in a matter of six quarters really turn around and improve the margins from maybe about 2%, and I am talking Software Services, maybe about 2% to 3% up to 11.5%, 12% EBIT." **Product Solutions margin is being compressed by pass-through economics** — the CFO's mechanism is precise and worth keeping: "memory pricing has an influence while we try and pass on everything to the customer. From a margin perspective, it affects because you do not get the same carry on the product as you would get earlier… you are passing on the cost, but the incremental margin does not come. So, from a percentage, it gets affected." The second driver is mix — Silicon "moving towards productization". On the headcount-vs-cost gap an analyst flagged (headcount +9%, cost +3%), the CFO attributed it to hiring mix (lateral + freshers), the non-recurring Q4 bonus catch-up, and improved utilization — "that is where you would have seen it not impacting the margins." Forward-looking cost adds already committed: "another five to six sales heads during the rest of the year".
capex / expansion (watch slippage): No capex number, no commissioning date and no capacity figure were disclosed on this call. Physical expansion named: **Sasken Silicon Incubation Center at Hubballi** (inaugurated, university collaboration) and a **new centre of excellence in Hyderabad** (opened). The only quantified balance-sheet consumption is working capital and fixed assets inside the cash-flow answer — "as we scale, there is going to be consumption in working capital as well as on FA" — plus a specific Q1 item: **"in Q1, we had to build some of the inventories in order to manage the memory shortage. So, in Q1, the cash flow impact is coming from there."**
capital allocation: The most checkable — and least comfortable — thread on the call. Operating cash flow has been **"negative for the last two years, despite profit growth"**, and management does not expect that to reverse this year: "We believe even this year we would have a large consumption of cash." The stated cause is growth investment, not collections: "It is not that we have had any challenges in our collections." Funding will be **"a mixture of our own internal accruals to finance the growth as well as external funds"** — i.e. external funding is now on the table for a company sitting on **₹356 Crores of cash and investments**. Asked whether Borqs is the sink, the CFO widened it: "It is just not Borqs, it is across as some of these engagements need working capital both in terms of capacity expansion as well as in terms of receivable and inventory." No dividend, buyback or debt commentary was offered. Inorganic spend remains possible ("we may look inorganic for our opportunities").
risks & watch-items:
- **Product Solutions margin at 5.9% with a contested bridge.** The 310bps-vs-690bps discrepancy (§2 box) means the size of the fall is not established. Management's own remedy is time, not action-specific: "we should look at the margins on a full year basis."
- **Memory shortage / component pricing is an active, unresolved input shock.** It hit margin (pass-through without carry), cash (inventory build) and, per Hareesh, customer behaviour — "on-device AI and memory supply pressure are reshaping product economics and encouraging customers to prioritize higher value enterprise and specialized devices."
- **Two years of negative operating cash flow, a third guided, plus "external funds."** With PAT at ₹23 Crores a quarter, an extended cash burn funded externally is the balance-sheet risk that most deserves next-quarter verification.
- **60x4x3 is slipping and management has softened it twice.** "Of course, three years was metaphoric. We may take maybe one or two more years." An analyst noted the $4m-plus customer count "has been at six for four consecutive quarters" — the count has not moved in a year while the deadline has.
- **Concentration is rising, not falling.** Top-5 at ~56% (analyst: up from 52%) — the *opposite* of what an account-broadening mission should produce, even as total customers went 79 → 93.
- **Disclosure opacity.** No vertical/offering revenue split ("We do not disclose number based on offerings or verticals"), no order backlog, no silicon production-vs-services split, no guidance, and no quantification of the foundry certifications. An analyst said so directly: "most of the IT companies would disclose their revenue segments it would be great if in future we can have that disclosure also."
- **Foundry certifications are unverifiable.** Intel and TSMC status is "in progress… we cannot specifically make any announcements on those yet."
- **Two-wheeler module opportunity is stuck on cost, not capability.** "We have the module ready, but then because of the cost, which the Quectel of the world gives, they are very cost sensitive, and they are taking it from China. So, we will have to see if there is any movement which will prevent them from importing these Chinese modules." The trigger is policy, and it is outside Sasken's control.
- **AI as a deflator of the headcount→revenue link.** "Headcount may not be the only vector to measure growth. So that will morph and we will have to look at how other metrics can be used" — the traditional visibility proxy for a services business is being retired without a replacement metric offered.
management quality / tone: Notably more open than the disclosure record suggests: Mody opened by saying the company deliberately started these quarterly calls because "we felt it equally important to strengthen how we engage with the investment community" — this is a company newly courting the market, and the analyst list (Niveshaay, Vallum, Nuvama AMC, Bowhead, CARE PMS, TPF, ithought) reflects that. Candour is real on the awkward items: the 60x4x3 timeline slip was conceded unprompted; the negative cash flow was answered directly with the cause and the funding plan rather than deflected; and Hareesh gave a genuinely unflattering answer on two-wheeler modules (ready product, losing on Chinese cost). Against that: the answers thin out precisely where numbers would bind — no segment splits, no backlog, no guidance, no margin trajectory, no quantification of the hyperscaler engagements or the foundry certifications, and Mody's answer on *how* 60x4x3 gets achieved was explicitly withheld ("I may not be able to describe that fully to you in absolute black and white"). One reply drifted into promotional register — "your Company today is more broad-based" — without answering the analyst's actual question on revenue contribution by offering.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The growth is now organic, and that is the buried headline.** The CFO's reconciliation is the cleanest fact on the call: end-Q1 FY26 headcount 2,200 **already included** the ~300 Borqs people, and today's 2,658 means **"all of that growth is actually organic addition to headcount."** The 24% YoY revenue growth is therefore no longer an acquisition artefact — this is the first quarter where that can be said cleanly.
- **The margin problem and the strategic win are the same event.** Silicon "moving towards productization" is exactly what management wants (product ownership, longer programs) *and* is a named cause of the Product Solutions margin fall. Rising product mix will keep depressing percentage margin even when it is creating value — the wrong metric will look wrong for a while.
- **Pass-through protects revenue and destroys margin percentage.** Memory cost is passed on in full, so revenue is inflated by cost the company doesn't earn on. Product Solutions' +23.6% YoY revenue growth is, to an unquantified degree, memory price inflation flowing through — and the same mechanism is what drags the margin percentage down. Both segments printing "+20%+" is less clean than it reads.
- **Sasken is short-tenor by design and knows it.** TCV ≈ one quarter of revenue with a 9–10-month backlog carry means the sales engine must be refilled continuously; the 60x4x3 account-mining mission is the structural answer to that, which is why the slipping timeline matters more than it would at a peer with multi-year annuity contracts.
- **The Qualcomm reference-design story is a moat *and* a leak.** Sasken built the two-wheeler instrument-cluster reference design; "Qualcomm took it and gave it to all the module suppliers", and Quectel-type module makers built around it. Sasken created the IP and Chinese module makers monetise the volume — a precise illustration of why management wants to move from services to owned modules.
- **Top-5 concentration rising while customer count rises is the tell.** 79 → 93 customers but 52% → ~56% top-5 share means the large accounts are growing faster than the long tail — good for revenue quality, but it is the reverse of the 60x4x3 thesis of lifting the *middle* of the base to $4m.
- **AI is being sold as both the product and the delivery method.** "A large part of our business gets delivered through a combination of headcount and AI" — an ER&D firm using AI to deliver fixed-scope work is deliberately shrinking its own billable-hours base, which is why the headcount metric is being pre-emptively retired.
